page.title: Advanced Article and Quantifier Nuance
page.subtitle_html: Advanced Article and Quantifier Nuance - C1 article choice, abstract nouns, and precise quantifier meaning.
page.subtitle_text: C1 article choice, abstract nouns, and precise quantifier meaning.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Advanced Article and Quantifier Nuance: compact anchors for precise article and quantifier meaning.","rules":[{"label":"Quantifier nuance","text":"Choose little, a little, few, a few, much, many, and several according to exact meaning and tone.","example":"There is little evidence to support this claim."},{"label":"Article choice","text":"Use a, the, or zero article to control whether a noun is general, specific, countable, or institutional.","example":"The research focuses on education policy."},{"label":"Formal precision","text":"In C1 writing, article and quantifier choices often change the strength of a claim.","example":"A number of issues remain unresolved."}]}

blocks.heading: C1 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder C1 advanced article and quantifier nuance lesson package.

page.title: Precision With Articles And Determiners
page.subtitle_html: Precision With Articles And Determiners - C2 control of articles, zero article, quantifiers, and reference.
page.subtitle_text: C2 control of articles, zero article, quantifiers, and reference.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Precision with articles and determiners: compact C2 anchors for generic meaning, specific reference, and nuanced quantity.","rules":[{"label":"Generic vs specific","text":"Choose zero article, a/an, or the according to whether the noun is general, introduced, or already identifiable.","example":"Research shows that sleep affects memory."},{"label":"Determiner nuance","text":"Use some, any, each, every, both, either, and neither to control scope and emphasis.","example":"Some evidence seems convincing."},{"label":"Reference control","text":"Use determiners to signal what the reader can already identify.","example":"The evidence presented here remains limited."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on precision with articles and determiners.

page.title: Advanced Collocation And Lexical Choice
page.subtitle_html: Advanced Collocation And Lexical Choice - C2 collocations for precise academic and professional phrasing.
page.subtitle_text: C2 collocations for precise academic and professional phrasing.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Advanced collocation and lexical choice: compact anchors for choosing precise verb-noun and adjective-noun combinations.","rules":[{"label":"Verb-noun collocations","text":"Use combinations such as pose a challenge, set a precedent, and draw a distinction when the noun expects a specific verb.","example":"This decision poses a significant challenge."},{"label":"Lexical precision","text":"Choose words that match the strength and register of the claim.","example":"The report identifies a substantial gap in provision."},{"label":"Formal register","text":"Prefer stable academic collocations over literal word-for-word alternatives.","example":"The case raises important questions about accountability."}]}
